identity: An Egyptian children-magazine COMIC PAGE, two strips back to back. Strip 1: a masthead (كسلان جدا يقدم بكل فخر) over the serial title ليلة بعد ليلة بعد ليلة, the episode label الليلة السادسة عشرة, and a two-field credit box (سيناريو أحمد محمد / رسوم مصطفى رحمة); then a Shahrazad-frame undersea tale in which Prince Hamur, the morning after his wedding, reforms the schools of مملكة البحار (computers in every school, three meals a day, sports, no beating pupils), banters with his wife, and is finally interrupted by a rooster (كوكو كوكو) who has wandered in and is spoiling the story the author is writing. Strip 2: a separate gag page credited كاريكاتير عمرو سليم, with a setup caption about أبو قردان wanting to change his name, four zoo panels (office, birth, waiting, congratulations-twins), and a one-panel caveman gag العصر البدائي. Register = my doctrine §T (comic strips / speech balloons) with §A front matter (masthead + credit fields) at the head of each strip.
law: The unit system here is LAYOUT, not syntax, so almost every boundary is free. Each <NL> line is exactly one panel caption, one speech balloon, one drawn sign, or one credit field, and each is one segment (T-1: one balloon = one segment). All 34 pre-<NL> tokens plus the final token are boundaries. Inside a line the default is WELD (LAW 0-double-prime) and I cut only where I can name the typographic reason: (1) a distinct FRONT-MATTER LAYOUT SLOT — series title vs episode label, script credit vs art credit — is its own segment (§A3 credit lines are one segment each, §J5 labels); (2) a BARE one-word interjection with no vocative attached is its own segment (H3/T-2, the single most reliable positive cut cue outside <NL>); (3) two COMPLETE printed sentences sharing one balloon — a question then a reproach, an exclamation then a reproach, a blessing repeated verbatim — are two segments (LAW 0-prime: ؟ and ! at the end of a real sentence; LAW 3 surviving carve-out for repeated complete exclamations). Everything else welds: و, ف, relative clauses, asyndetic descriptive continuations, a vocative or answer-particle fused to the statement it introduces, a doubled onomatopoeia, and a trailing vocative.
reasoning: STEP 1 — take the free boundaries. 34 <NL> tokens plus the final token = 35 mandated cuts, taken in full (the <NL> prior is 100 percent over 41 documents). But الليلة السادسة عشرة is an episode label, a separate layout slot, and §A3 says such fields are one segment each. Marked lo because §T @32 (مسابقة الطفل الجميل كوب حليب مجانا لكل الأطفال) shows a two-slot drawn sign welding, and this could be the same phenomenon. @16 محمد, CUT, med. سيناريو أحمد محمد and رسوم مصطفى رحمة are two credit boxes printed side by side, i.e. two cells (§J2). §A1 batch-2 gold shows a credit field is exactly one segment (ترجمة د دانا شاكر ‖, مراجعة د أحمد خريس ‖). Note I do NOT cut after the labels سيناريو or رسوم themselves — a label welds to its name, same law that welds ترجمة to د دانا شاكر. @57 line, WELD. نعم يا مولاي الجميع في انتظار تشريفكم في قاعة الاجتماعات الكبرى: near-verbatim precedent in §U doc_2baf8d2ac98d @28, gold نعم يا سيدي هذا هو قصر أمير المؤمنين, welded. T-1 @127 (يا إلهي لا أستطيع منح الجائزة) welds a vocative to its statement too. Same ruling at @148-154 آسف يا مولاتي عندي اجتماع في المساء. @162 العزيز, CUT, lo — my least certain cut. كان الله في عونك يا زوجي العزيز / كان الله في عونك is a verbatim repetition of a complete finite blessing-sentence. Two identical finite clauses cannot be printed adjacent with nothing between them, so a mark was there, and in a comic balloon a doubled exclamation takes .. or ! far more often than ،. This is LAW 3's surviving carve-out (أنا أقوى الأقوياء ‖ أنا عظيم العظماء ‖), the one asyndetic pattern batch 2 did not kill. The vocative attaches to the FIRST blessing, which is the natural Arabic order, so the cut falls after العزيز and not earlier. T-1 would weld this whole line; I accept the risk. @184 هنا, CUT, med. كيف ظهرت هنا is a complete interrogative clause, so its ؟ is a LAW 0-prime end mark, and ستفسد القصة التي أؤلفها is a second and different illocutionary act. T8 warns that questions weld inside interior monologue and inside scripture, but this is dialogue, where §O2 cuts each question inside speech. @231 مبروك, CUT, med. A bare one-word interjection with NO vocative attached — the exact register-and-shape twin of doc_4114b13808e9 @111, gold حسنا ‖ خذ المزيد منه ‖, which my doctrine calls my most reliable positive cut cue outside <NL> and which was a MISS last time. The discriminator I am applying across this whole document: a bare interjection alone cuts (مبروك, حسنا), an interjection or answer-particle bound to a vocative welds forward (نعم يا مولاي, آسف يا مولاتي, يا إلهي). @240 قطا, CUT, med. هذا ليس قطا (rejection) and قلت لك ألف مرة أن القط يقول مياو (reproach) are two asyndetic INDEPENDENT FINITE clauses. Asyndeton between two full finite clauses with different illocutionary force is the strongest available evidence of a printed stop, and is not the participial/descriptive chaining that welds in §P1.
